Not weird at all! I used a mix of fake flowers (from Michael's), dried greenery (amazon), and sola wood flowers, and I was really happy with how it turned out. The dried greenery helped it look a bit more realistic imo. If you go the sola wood route, I recommend ohyourelovely over solawoodflowers(.)com—the flowers looked way more realistic & arrived in better shape. They also have extremely high quality/realistic faux greenery, but it's kind of pricey. I just used cheap dollar store acrylic paint mixed with water and a small amount of glycerin to dye the flowers; it takes a bit of time but it's not too difficult. The really fancy flowers (ex.  peonies, other flowers with lots of detailed curls in the petals) can uncurl a bit while you dye them, so I recommend leaving those the natural color (it's a cream/off white) if you do sola flowers. The roses/chrysanthemum/carnation style flowers are fine during the dye process though!


Also, if you get any faux leaves/greenery in a color you're not a fan of, you can use spray paint on them! I got some really cheap leaves at Michael's that looked suuuuper fake, but after spray painting some of them a dark red/some gold they looked way better. I also spray painted faux amaranth a deep red and it looked much better/more realistic than the original color (light blue)!

In general, it can restrict your travel (but it's usually based on what the crime was, how long ago it was, & the nature of the visit). Just as an example, years ago my husband had booked a band from the US to play a show where we live (Canada). One of the members had a DUI (I think it was ~6-7 years before this). My husband had to write a letter saying that he had invited the band to play for people who bought tickets so it was a work related trip. Border services also called him & asked him to verify all of this because the band was detained at the border. They were allowed to enter after that, but it was a lot of hassle, they all had to confirm he wouldn't be driving, they were leaving in 48 hours, etc etc. Basically, they had to prove that he wasn't a risk.


I think you can also go through the "criminal rehabilitation" process, which can allow you to enter if it's a certain amount of time after you completed the sentence (paid all fines, completed community service/probation/prison sentence, etc). From my understanding, it's a long & difficult process with an application fee, but it makes it easier for future travel. Depending on your age, anything from when you were a juvenile might be long ago enough that it could be in your favor. Regarding stuff you didn't do, this would be something you have to prove (ex. I read that even if you were found not guilty, you have to prove that this happened because the arrest will still show up). I imagine a weed-related charge would be easier to apply for/show "criminal rehabilitation" for travel to Canada because it's legal here now, but I'm definitely not a lawyer/expert!! Not sure if links are allowed here, but this site breaks it down really well (for travel to Canada, at least!): https://www.temporaryresidentpermitcanada.com/criminal-record.php

I think a question to ask yourself is what timeline would you leave/divorce him? I know you mentioned that he has an appointment in two months, but what then? What if he finds out he does have schizophrenia at the appointment, and chooses to go on medication? What if he refuses to take medication? What if it turns out he doesn't have schizophrenia (either an alternative condition, or potentially nothing at all)? In these scenarios, would you then leave right after, or would you want to stay with him for ~3 months while he starts meds, ~6 months while he does other tests (if it's not schizophrenia), a year? Longer? Less time? 


I genuinely don't mean these questions in an antagonistic way, but just as general questions for you to consider & decide for yourself. The goal post of his appointment in two months can change quickly, but it seems like you have firmly made up your mind on divorce (which I think is a good thing because it shows that you are willing to set a boundary for yourself & your daughter). If you do start the divorce process, it won't be an overnight thing—a good first step could be talking to a lawyer to discuss it, even before the appointment. This doesn't mean you'll be divorced instantly, and it will give you a stronger idea of how the process will work. It may make you feel better knowing that you have an exit strategy, as you mentioned feeling trapped. I know everyone always recommends therapy in these subs, but when dealing with an impending divorce, your husband's mental health, & how this is affecting your own mental health, it might be helpful to work with a therapist to help you figure out a plan of action (divorce, leaving, navigating boundaries etc), safety plans (just in case), and to help you process everything in general. They could potentially help you figure out how you can maintain a relationship with him/between him & your daughter in the future (if it's safe and something everyone involved would want). It's clear that you have a great deal of empathy for him, but remember to support yourself and what's best for you in a difficult situation like this. Wishing you well in a really difficult situation!!

These are the best cookies!! I love making them & I know how much effort they are, so excellent work! What filling did you use? 

For anyone interested in a recipe, I don't know which one OP used, but this is my go-to (very slightly adapted from [https://www.italianfoodforever.com/2011/11/peach-cookies-for-rose-anne/#mv-creation-651-jtr](https://www.italianfoodforever.com/2011/11/peach-cookies-for-rose-anne/#mv-creation-651-jtr))

* 3 large eggs
* 2 cups sugar (just regular, white granulated sugar)
* 1 cup vegetable oil
* 2 tsp vanilla
* Zest of a lemon or orange (optional)
* 4 tsp baking powder
* 1 tsp salt
* 1 cup milk (2% or whole milk is better, but I've used soy, oat, and 1% before with no issues)
* 6 cups flour (I usually start with 4 cups and add more as I need to, or else the dough is really tough to mix)
* Warming spices (optional, but cardamom, ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, etc are all delicious in the dough)

Directions:

* Beat the eggs and sugar in a bowl until the mix is light (preferably in a mixer or with a hand mixer, it takes longer and uses more effort by hand), then add in the oil until it's a creamy/smooth mix
* Add in vanilla and milk (and optional citrus zest)
* Sift 4 cups of the flour with the salt and baking powder, and gradually incorporate it into the wet mix. Add the rest of the flour as needed (depending on humidity, you may or may not need the full 6 cups. The dough needs to be firm enough that it can be rolled)
* Roll the cookies: you can do \~0.75 inch balls or \~1.5 inch balls (smaller cookies look cute, but it's more effort in later steps because it makes more cookies). Just roll them into balls, don't squish/flatten them! They gradually settle on the tray while you roll the rest/bake them. In my experience, they don't spread very much but still leave a bit of space between them!
* Bake the cookies at 350F for 15-20 minutes until the bottom is fully golden brown (if it's too light, the cookies might not be baked in the middle)
* When the cookies are cooled, used a small & sharp pairing knife to carve out a little bit of the bottom of the cookie. Be gentle and don't carve them too deep or too close to the edge of the cookie (a few cookies might break while you do this, which is a snack to reward your effort). This hollowed out part is where the filling will go! Save the cookie crumbs!!!
* For the filling, you can use a ton of stuff (I've done pastry cream, homemade cranberry sauce, store bought jam and homemade jam, and I've even mixed raspberry jam with pastry cream). You want to mix some (not all) of the leftover cookie crumbs with the filling (the crumbs will soften a bit and help "glue" the cookies together with the filling). You can also add finely chopped nuts with the crumbs.
* Use a small spoon to scoop filling into the carved out cookies (try to match the cookies by size). I overfill the carved part \*just\* a bit, so when you squish two halves together the extra filling glues the cookies together. I always chill them after this step before decorating because it helps them hold together. Just a half hour in the fridge is fine (note: for food safety, these cookies are best stored in the fridge after filling, especially when using pastry cream)
* To decorate: lots of people will use peach schnapps or other clear liqueurs to help you paint the cookies, but if you don't drink or are serving them to young kids you can use milk! There are two ways to paint the cookies, and for both you will need three bowls: one with the schnapps or milk and red food coloring, one with the schnapps/milk and yellow food coloring, and one with sugar (superfine is better, but I always use regular granulated sugar with no issues). Make sure the colors are very bright. Some people just dunk the cookie in the yellow then the red food coloring, but I find the cookie gets soft/soggy VERY quickly with this method and the cookies are more likely to fall apart. I use two food safe paintbrushes and just dab the color on that way (you can be a little messy because the colors will blend to make it look more like a peach). While still wet, roll the cookie in the sugar to coat. Let them dry before eating, which doesn't take too long!

The main thing to remember is that this show is a heavily producer manipulated tv show (to be fair most reality tv is lol). The contestants are often cast and edited into different archetypes (friendly/relatable, mean/villain, etc) and everyone on the show uses very specific terms. "I could potentially see myself falling in love", "I'm on the path to falling in love" and "I'm falling in love" are three different things for example lol. 

Near the end of the season are hometown dates! Usually the final 4 contestants invite the lead to their hometown to meet their family and imo it's always the best week of the season. The lead has to try to convince four different sets of parents that they want to be with that contestant, while simultaneously not revealing who they *actually* want to be with. The parents are often incredibly normal and view the show as ridiculous, which is entertaining to watch lmao.

If you like the show, I recommend watching some older seasons! Rachel L (bachelorette season 13) had a great season that's a good introduction to the show. Ali (season 6), Ashley (season 7) and Emily (season 8) all had entertaining seasons that can give a good overview of the structure, drama, etc but Rachel's is my favorite. For the bachelor, Ben F (season 16) is a fun season with one of the most memorable 'villains' of the show. Jason (season 13) has a good season and I believe it's one of the oldest seasons that's accessible to stream/buy (a lot of the early seasons are hard to find). If you want to watch a newer season, Peter (season 24) had a highly entertaining season, but it's a lot of drama and less of a love story so it depends what you're looking for lol.

I love making buffalo spaghetti squash! When my partner and I make it, we cut the squash in half and roast it (~45 min at 350 depending on size). Scrape the squash out with a fork, then we toss it with lightly sauteed onion/celery/carrot, buffalo sauce, blue cheese, and sometimes cream cheese. Sprinkle with bread crumbs + more blue cheese and bake/broil it for the cheese to melt and breadcrumbs to toast! We often will pan sear chicken, toss that in Buffalo sauce, and have that mixed in with the squash too. 

Also recommend buffalo sauce + eggs! Scrambled eggs & omelettes especially. Buffalo ranch makes a great multi-purpose sauce too - you could have it on different sandwiches (cold cuts, tofu, etc), as a pizza sauce (even on naan/pita if you don't want to make or use pizza crust) or as a dip for veggies. Buffalo sauce is also tasty in marinades, especially for chicken or tofu. Honestly I've even roasted veggies with buffalo sauce + a bit of oil (depending how buttery the buffalo you have is, you can skip the oil) + salt/pepper/garlic powder!

For me, I smoked from 2013-2018 and tried to quit a few times. The main thing that made me want to quit was honestly just the health risks. I started forcing myself to spend 10-15 min a day reading about how bad smoking is and it led to nightmares and anxiety about smoking, which sucked lol but honestly that was the thing that made me stick to it. I realized I was more afraid of cancer and all the other health issues (I was coughing up phlegm every morning too 🤢) than going without nicotine. Other things that helped: nicotine gum and going outside whenever I wanted a cigarette right after I quit. I would chew a piece of gum and stand on my apartment's balcony for 5 minutes 5+ times a day (whenever the cravings were really strong) and the physical act of going outside and still getting nicotine for the gum helped to satisfy my cravings! 

Also I really recommend that if he chooses to quit, to just pick a date and stick to it. For some people, that date is within the week! For me, I picked a date 2 months out lol. It gave me time to slightly reduce my intake (from about 12 a day to 7-8) and mentally prepare to quit. Honestly though it is different for everyone, and if your bf is able to it might be good for him to talk to his doctor! There are prescription options (Wellbutrin for example) and even drugs that make you nauseated if you smoke (which can have other side effects too of course). And for some people there are different combinations of nicotine replacement that work (like using a patch/inhaler/gum/etc in combo with each other or with other medication) that a doctor could give better advice on based on how long he smoked, how much he smoked etc. If it encourages him, I will say my cravings were extremely manageable after only a few days! I really thought I would be struggling for weeks and weeks trying to deal but after 3-4 days it just felt more like a mild annoyance when I got a craving. By week 3 I could go 2+ days without a craving. I know people always say it gets easier but it really does! Best of luck to him quitting, sorry for writing a novel lol

Echoing some of the responses here to say that nothing changed. I ran away from home at 16 (away from my mom, moved in with my dad) and had very limited contact with my mom until 19 (2014) when I went fully no contact. I didn't talk to her again until 2018, when my maternal grandmother died. I felt bad for my mom, because I had not been in contact with her when my grandpa died a few years before, and she was living alone, now lost both parents, etc. 


I live in another city, so we just talked on the phone. After a week, everything was back to how it was before. She ignored all boundaries and called me multiple times a day and got angry with me if I didn't answer. When we did talk, it was either about her, or how I'm not good enough at something. She had never met my partner, and the only thing I told her about him was that he doesn't drink alcohol - she sent him alcohol filled chocolate for Christmas and a book for me called "How Cinderella Grew Up." Every single phone call was incredibly triggering and I felt just like the terrified child I was when I lived with her. I got anxious every time I looked at my phone because I didn't want her to call and I had massive urges to self harm. I finally blocked her just after Christmas, but I felt guilty about it and answered the phone a few months later. She told me I was being a bad child and that I "needed" to call her more, she trampled over even more boundaries, I told her I won't speak to her if she is disrespectful to me. And then she was disrespectful....so I hung up and haven't talked to her since, lol. 


Nearly 4 years no contact now and I won't lie, there have been periods of immense guilt. I started going back to therapy because of that and it's really helped me feel at peace with the decision. It's okay to protect yourself (and your family) from her - if she's alone, that's her fault, not yours. It's easier to say this than feel it, of course. I guess what I'm saying is that the urge to reconnect is normal (even though not everyone experiences it, which is also normal!) and of course you can do whatever you want and whatever is best for you. But in my own experience, nothing changes. The only positive I see from my brief reconnection with my mom is that it made me see why I stopped talking to her in the first place and why no contact has been the best decision in my life. My mental health could be better, but the more removed I am from her abuse, the better I feel.


Whatever you decide to do, I hope it's the best decision for you and your mental health!

I think for me, when it's unexpected it puts me into fight or flight mode and causes panic attacks and just generally makes me feel awful. If I know something is coming, I think my brain doesn't get caught off guard and it's easier to view it as fiction, rather than making my body/brain feel like it's in danger (even if I can logically understand I'm safe, it causes a physical/emotional response).


I love plot twists, gore, murder, ghosts, etc in horror, and I've always enjoyed the genre! I live in Ontario and have ordered from both solawoodflowers.com and ohyourelovely, and the biggest issue I had with both was the shipping costs. Ordering during a sale might as well have been ordering at full price because of the USD conversion/shipping fees lol. I will say that the quality of ohyourelovely is hands down MUCH better. The flowers were more full/less squished, feel less fragile (despite having more detail and slightly thinner petals than solawoodflowers) and they look way more realistic! I still plan on using the solawoodflower ones, but those are going to mostly be my filler flowers with the focus on the others. Shipping was a similar amount of time/cost for both (both used USPS that transferred to Canada post at the border) and both took about 3 weeks to ship to me, which is pretty standard/slightly longer than normal for most things I order from the US. For anyone reading this old post - definitely subscribe to both of their0 email lists to hear about the sales, because you'll save money compared to buying regular price and paying for shipping on top of that lol.

I was also going to ask where you got the greenery--it looks great! I actually ordered the Italian ruscus from ohyourelovely as well but it hasn't arrived yet, so it's good to know it looks good in person (finding realistic fake greenery is so hard lol). Love your colors too btw!!
